customer_name: Chinese Academy of Sciences (中国科学院)
business_problem: Ecology researchers needed a lighter, more scalable way to identify species and monitor field conditions because manual biodiversity observation and pest counting required heavy equipment, expert interpretation, and long collection cycles.
solution_summary: Researchers associated with the Chinese Academy of Sciences used Baidu Brain capabilities to turn biodiversity observation into an AI-assisted workflow. The core implementation is the 'BioNote' platform, which lets field staff or the public photograph species and immediately retrieve likely identifications along with time, location, and habitat information, replacing much of the manual note-taking and equipment burden of traditional surveys. The broader collaboration also drew in speech recognition for hands-free data capture and machine-learning support for related ecological monitoring work such as insect and pest counting, showing how Baidu's AI stack could extend beyond image recognition into field-data collection and ecosystem management. What matters most is that the system transformed observation from a specialist-only task into a participatory digital workflow: researchers get faster recognition and recording, while citizen users can contribute new training data through the mobile app, making biodiversity monitoring more scalable over time.

solution_components.name: BioNote AI Platform
solution_components.role: Lets researchers and the public identify species from photos and capture structured field-observation records.

solution_components.name: Image Search
solution_components.role: Supports visual species recognition from field photographs.

solution_components.name: Speech Recognition
solution_components.role: Allows field observers to record contextual information without manual typing.

solution_components.name: PaddlePaddle Integrated Machine
solution_components.role: Provides local AI support for broader ecological monitoring work such as insect-pest counting and model experimentation.

data_flow: Species photos and field observations are captured in BioNote, passed through image-recognition services, and returned with likely identifications plus time and habitat context. Additional speech input can record observations hands-free, and related ecological monitoring projects reuse AI infrastructure for tasks such as pest counting and species-pattern analysis.
business_outcome: The ecology teams reduced manual field effort, improved the speed of species identification and ecological monitoring, and opened biodiversity data collection to broader public participation.
metrics: Public participation in scientific observation increased significantly through the mobile app.
architecture_clues: The workflow combines image recognition, speech capture, and citizen-contributed mobile uploads rather than keeping observation inside specialist field equipment only.
The same AI foundation is reused for biodiversity identification and related pest-monitoring scenarios.
BioNote is designed as both a research tool and a public contribution channel for future model learning.
evidence_quotes: Researcher Lin Congtian used Baidu Brain to create the 'BioNote' AI platform for biodiversity work (original: 林聪田开始利用百度大脑开放平台探索在物种多样性领域的开发与创新，研发出一个名为"生物记"的人工智能平台).
Field staff can photograph a species and immediately record time, exact location, and habitat information through BioNote (original: 当一位野外工作人员拍下一张照片时，他就能随时通过"生物记"去快速识别，并记录物种出现的时间、精确的位置信息及生存环境信息).
The team also planned to let bird enthusiasts upload photos through the BioNote app to add training data (original: 鼓励鸟类爱好者将拍摄到的图片上传到 App 里…既能增加可以训练的数据).
In the related pest-monitoring work, data could be collected hourly instead of weekly and accuracy exceeded 90% (original: 以前一周统计一次的数据现在已经可以实现一小时一次，而且准确率更是达到了90%以上).
